# wallix.bastion.usergroup

Manage user groups on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.0.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete a user group on a WALLIX Bastion.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_usergroup` Terraform resource.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-description"></a>**description** | `str` | Description of the group. |
| <a id="parameter-group-name"></a>**group_name** | `str` / required | Name of the user group. Identifies the group on the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-profile"></a>**profile** | `str` | Name of the profile given to the members of the group. |
| <a id="parameter-restrictions"></a>**restrictions** | `list / elements=dict` | Session restrictions applied to the members of the group. Order does not matter.<br>When set, replaces all the restrictions of the group. Use `[]` to remove all restrictions. |
| <a id="parameter-restrictions-action"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **action** | `str` / required | What to do when the rule matches.<br><br>Choices: `kill`, `notify` |
| <a id="parameter-restrictions-rules"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **rules** | `str` / required | Regular expression matched against the session traffic. |
| <a id="parameter-restrictions-subprotocol"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **subprotocol** | `str` / required | Subprotocol the rule applies to.<br><br>Choices: `SSH_SHELL_SESSION`, `SSH_REMOTE_COMMAND`, `SSH_SCP_UP`, `SSH_SCP_DOWN`, `SFTP_SESSION`, `RLOGIN`, `TELNET`, `RDP` |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Whether the group should exist.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-timeframes"></a>**timeframes** | `list / elements=str` | Names of the timeframes during which the members of the group can connect, for example `allthetime`. Order does not matter.<br>Required when the group does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state). |
| <a id="parameter-users"></a>**users** | `list / elements=str` | Names of the users that belong to the group. Order does not matter.<br>When set, replaces all the members of the group. Use `[]` to remove every member.<br>Membership can also be managed from the user with [`wallix.bastion.user`](user.md) `groups`; set it on one side only. |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- The group is looked up by [`group_name`](#parameter-group-name), so it cannot be renamed with this module.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Ensure a group of Linux administrators exists
  wallix.bastion.usergroup:
    group_name: linux-admins
    description: Administrators of the Linux servers
    timeframes: [allthetime]
    users: [john.doe, jane.doe]
    restrictions:
      - action: kill
        rules: "rm -rf /"
        subprotocol: SSH_SHELL_SESSION

- name: Remove every member of a group
  wallix.bastion.usergroup:
    group_name: linux-admins
    users: []

- name: Remove a group
  wallix.bastion.usergroup:
    group_name: linux-admins
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the group already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["users"]` |
| <a id="return-usergroup"></a>**usergroup** | `dict` | The user group as returned by the Bastion API after the change, restrictions without their ids.<br>In check mode, the expected group. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-usergroup) |

<a id="sample-usergroup"></a>

### Sample of `usergroup`

```yaml
description: Administrators of the Linux servers
email_list: ''
group_name: linux-admins
id: 1a0f6dae63280cc2005056b66c8b
language: en
profile: null
restrictions:
- action: kill
  rules: rm -rf /
  subprotocol: SSH_SHELL_SESSION
timeframes:
- allthetime
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/usergroups/1a0f6dae63280cc2005056b66c8b
users:
- john.doe
- jane.doe
```
